en.title: Distinct Averages from Pairing Experience Values at Both Ends
en.description:
Repeatedly pair the people with the smallest and the largest remaining experience into a group and remove both, until everyone is paired. Find the number of distinct values among the groups' average experience.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains an even n; the second line contains the experience values. 2≤n≤100000 and n is even; 1≤experience≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
hints: Sort, pair the two ends moving inward, and put each pair's sum into a set. Two averages are equal exactly when the two sums are equal, so no floating point is needed.
